choices: Oil furnace (an oil tank, often in the basement or outside)

nodes.title: Natural gas or propane?
nodes.body: Natural gas comes through a meter, usually on an outside wall. Propane comes from a tank in the yard that a supplier fills.
choices: A tank-gauge check can come later.
That's fine. We'll skip fuel checks.

nodes.title: What kind of home is it?
nodes.body: Manufactured homes (single-wide, double-wide) use furnaces and ducts built for them, so some checks differ.
choices: A house built on site, a condo, or a townhouse
Built in a factory on a steel frame.

nodes.title: (unchanged)
nodes.body: (unchanged)
choices: A light is blinking or a code is showing on the furnace
Read it before anything else. Don't turn the power off.
Heat stopped during or after snow, ice, or a storm
Outdoor vent pipes can get blocked.
Heat loss after snow or ice reported.
One end or area of the home stays cold
Propane or oil may be low or out
(router) propane → fn.fuel.propane_gauge; oil → fn.fuel.oil_tank; else hidden
Shown only for propane or oil.
The furnace is new and the thermostat doesn't work right with it
New furnace with thermostat trouble reported.

nodes.title: Look at the furnace light
nodes.body: Most furnaces have a small window or peephole in the lower door with a light behind it. Some show a code on a display or on the thermostat. Look only. Don't remove the door or turn the power off first: on some furnaces that erases the code.

step.what: Reading the light changes nothing on the furnace.
step.caution: Removing the door or cutting power can erase the stored code on some brands.
step.source: From Carrier 58-3T service label p.4 and ICP 441 01 2023 01 p.38, checked 2026-10-11.
steps: Stand in front of the furnace and find the small window in the lower door.
Watch the light for one full minute.
Count the flashes, or write down what the display shows. A phone video helps.
step.watch: One minute. Codes repeat with a pause between them.
step.stop: Stop if you smell gas or burning, hear a CO alarm, or see water near wires.

choices: It blinks a pattern, or shows letters or numbers
Blinking light or code seen through the window.
It's on steady, or blinks slowly and evenly
Steady means different things by brand.
No window, or I can't see it

nodes.title: What brand is on the furnace?
nodes.body: Look for the name on the front of the furnace or near the window. Codes vary by model and control board, so if the code chart on your furnace says something different from ours, trust the chart.
choices: Oil furnace: the light is on the oil burner control
Another brand, or I can't tell

nodes.title: Which one matches?
nodes.body: Pick what you see. If none match, pick "Not listed".  Then the display line for the family (see §4).
choices: Code <code> (<meaning>) read through the window. Power not cut.
Not listed, or I'm not sure

nodes.title: Before you go outside, check these
nodes.body: Plastic vent pipes on an outside wall can get buried by snow. First make sure going outside is safe.
choices: A CO alarm is sounding, or anyone has headache, dizziness, or nausea
Get everyone out to fresh air.
CO alarm or symptoms at the outdoor check.
Rotten-egg or gas smell, inside or outside
Gas smell at the outdoor check.
The house is getting cold and someone's at risk
Cold-exposure risk at the outdoor check. (reuses gate cold_exposure_911 unchanged)
The gas meter or propane tank regulator is buried or iced
Meter or regulator buried or iced.
The furnace pipes are high up or above the house, out of reach from the ground
Ice, dark, or the storm makes it the wrong time to go out
No plastic pipes outside. The furnace vents through a metal pipe
Metal vent reported; no outdoor pipes to check.
None of these. I can safely reach the pipes from the ground

nodes.title: Clear snow from the furnace pipes
nodes.body: A high-efficiency furnace uses two white or gray plastic pipes on an outside wall: one brings air in, one sends exhaust out. If snow or ice covers either one, a safety switch shuts the furnace off.

step.what: Clearing snow from the outside of the pipes lets the furnace breathe again.
step.caution: Exhaust can be hot and wet. Damaging a pipe can let exhaust into the house.
step.source: From Enbridge Gas "Keep your gas meter clear" and Rheem R95T installation instructions (terminations at least 12 in. above snow level), checked 2026-10-11.
steps: Find both pipe ends on the outside wall.
Brush snow away by hand or with a soft broom. Clear a wide area around both pipes.
Leave any ice that's stuck to a pipe.
Keep shoveled or plowed snow away from the pipes.
step.watch: Watch for 15 minutes from inside for the furnace to start on its own.
step.stop: Stop if a pipe is cracked, loose, or apart, if ice is inside a pipe, or if a CO alarm sounds.

choices: Snow was blocking a pipe, and I cleared it
Snow found at a vent pipe; cleared by hand.
Ice is inside a pipe or frozen onto the end
Ice at vent pipe, not cleared.
A pipe is cracked, sagging, or pulled apart
I can't find or reach them safely

nodes.title: Give it time to restart
nodes.body: Many furnaces try again on their own once the pipes are clear. Some wait out a lockout first, about an hour on some brands and up to three hours on others. Watch from inside.
choices: The house is getting too cold, or someone's at risk
It started, then stopped with the same code
Still no heat after the wait

nodes.title: Look at the drain tube
nodes.body: High-efficiency furnaces make water. A clear or white tube carries it to a floor drain, a small pump, or outside. If it freezes or kinks, the furnace shuts off. Look from outside the furnace only.

step.what: Looking changes nothing. Straightening a kink in a tube you can reach without tools frees the water path.
step.caution: Pulling on a tube can pop it off and leak water.
step.source: From York/Coleman/Luxaire TM9E (pressure switches trip on a blocked condensate drain) and Rheem R95T p.9 (freeze protection), checked 2026-10-11.
steps: Follow the tube from the outside of the furnace to where it drains.
Look for ice, a kink, a sag full of water, or a beeping pump.
If a tube outside the furnace is kinked, gently straighten it by hand.
step.watch: Look for water on the floor over the next hour.
step.stop: Stop if the tube is frozen, cracked, or you'd need to open the furnace.

choices: Ice in the tube, or the outside drain end is frozen
A tube was kinked, and I straightened it by hand
A small pump is full, beeping, or overflowing
Water on the floor, away from wires
I can't see it without opening the furnace

nodes.title: Look at the furnace switch and breaker
nodes.body: Most furnaces have a nearby on/off switch that looks like a light switch. Then look at the breaker marked for the furnace. Look only for now.
choices: The furnace breaker is tripped (in the middle or off)
Furnace breaker looks tripped. Not reset.
I can't find or reach them safely

nodes.title: Was it turned off on purpose?
nodes.body: People turn a furnace switch off for repairs, leaks, or a smell, and sometimes by mistake for a light switch.
choices: Someone turned it off on purpose, or I'm not sure
It was turned off by mistake, and there's no smell, water, or noise

nodes.title: Turn the furnace switch back on, once
nodes.body: If nobody turned it off on purpose, you can turn it back on, one time only.
nodes.spec_note: Wave 1 never told anyone to touch this switch. Under pn-v1 §5 it is a homeowner-reachable switch outside the furnace, used once only after the intentional-off check (doctrine audit lesson f). The F11 regex must allow this one string id (see §8).

step.what: Turning the furnace switch back on gives the furnace power again.
step.caution: If something made the furnace unsafe, power lets it try to run.
step.source: From Trane "Furnace Not Igniting?" (check that the furnace switch is on), checked 2026-10-11.
steps: Set the thermostat to Heat.
Flip the furnace on/off switch to on, once.
Step back and wait.
step.watch: Watch for 15 minutes for warm air.
step.stop: Stop and turn it back off if you smell gas or burning, hear a bang, or a breaker trips.

choices: Switch turned on once; heat returned.
It shut off again, or a breaker tripped
Shut off again after one switch-on. reset_count=1

nodes.title: Read the propane tank gauge
nodes.body: The gauge is usually under the dome lid on top of the tank and reads percent full. Reading it is all you need to do.

step.caution: Opening the wrong cover or touching a valve can let gas out.
step.source: From PERC Safety Guide for Propane Users (2025), "Check the fuel gauge on your propane tank periodically", checked 2026-10-11.
steps: Lift the dome lid on top of the tank.
Read the number on the round gauge.
Close the lid.
step.stop: Stop if you smell gas or hear hissing. Leave the area and call your supplier or 911 from a safe place.

choices: It reads empty or near zero
I can't read it, or there's no gauge
I smell gas or hear hissing

nodes.title: Check the oil tank gauge
nodes.body: Many oil tanks have a gauge on top, often a clear tube with a float. Reading it is all you need to do. Don't press the red button on the oil burner.

step.caution: Pressing the burner's red button can flood it with oil.
step.source: From Thermo Pride OD6 manual (doc 1030), warning about the oil burner control's red button, checked 2026-10-11.
steps: Find the gauge on top of the tank.
Read where the float or needle sits.
step.stop: Stop if you smell oil or smoke, or see soot. Leave and call your oil service company.

nodes.title: Check how the filter fits
nodes.body: A clean filter can still choke airflow if it's the wrong size, doubled up, or in backward.

step.what: Fixing how the filter sits lets air through.
step.caution: Running with no filter lets dust into the furnace.
step.source: From NRCan Keeping the Heat In §9.1.1 and §9.1.4, and the filter sections of the Carrier 58-3T and Intertherm M7RL manuals, checked 2026-10-11.
steps: Check that the size printed on the filter matches the slot.
Check that only one filter is in the slot.
Check that the airflow arrow points toward the furnace.
Fix what's off, then close the cover.
step.stop: Stop if the filter slot needs tools or opens into the furnace.

choices: Something was off, and I fixed it

nodes.title: Check the furnace closet air path
nodes.body: Most manufactured-home furnaces pull room air in through louvers on the front or in the closet door, and many hold the filter on the inside of the front cover.

step.what: Clearing the air path lets the furnace pull in room air.
step.caution: A blocked door or closet can overheat the furnace and shut it off.
step.source: From Intertherm/Nordyne M1 (return air through the door louvers) and M7RL (filter on the door), and 24 CFR 3280.709/3280.715, checked 2026-10-11.
steps: Move anything stored in the furnace closet or against the louvered door.
Check that the grille and louvers aren't covered.
If the filter sits on the inside of the front cover and the cover lifts off without tools, look at it and replace it if it's dirty.
Check that inside doors have their gap at the bottom, not blocked by thick rugs.
step.stop: Stop if a door needs tools to open or you see wires.

choices: The filter was dirty, and I replaced it

nodes.title: Look at the crossover duct from outside
nodes.body: In a double-wide or triple-wide, a big round duct under the home carries heat between the halves. Look only from outside the skirting with a flashlight, through a vent or an open access panel. Don't crawl under the home.
choices: The duct is on the ground, crushed, torn, or loose
Crossover duct problem seen from outside.
I see or hear animals under the home
It looks connected and off the ground
I can't see it without going under

nodes.title: Feel the air at a vent
nodes.body: Electric furnaces turn their heaters on in steps after the fan starts. Set Heat above room temperature, then hold your hand near a vent for a few minutes.

step.source: From Nordyne E2 electric furnace manual (sequence of operation), checked 2026-10-11.
steps: Set the thermostat to Heat, a few degrees above the room.
Hold your hand near a vent for 3 to 5 minutes.
step.watch: 3 to 5 minutes (policy, not a maker figure).
step.stop: Stop if you smell burning or see smoke.

choices: Warm but weak, and rooms fall behind
The fan runs, but the air never warms
Look only. Big double breakers stay as they are.

nodes.title: Listen and feel at the vents
nodes.body: The blower moves air through the filter, the furnace or coil, and the ducts. Some motors ramp up slowly and quietly (ECM). Others start and stop all at once (PSC). Both are normal. Weak air usually means something is in the way: a dirty filter, closed vents, or blocked returns.

step.source: From NRCan Keeping the Heat In §9.1.4 (ECM and PSC motors) and 24 CFR 3280.715(a)(2), checked 2026-10-11.
steps: With heat on, listen near the indoor unit for the blower.
Hold your hand near two or three vents.
Count how many vents and return grilles are closed or covered.
step.stop: Stop if you smell burning or hear grinding or squealing.

choices: The blower runs, but air is weak
The blower never runs on a heat call
It's a heat pump air handler, and the outdoor unit runs
HP lane entry (same target as furnace_plus_heat_pump)
Heat pump checks take it from here.
HP air handler; handed to the HP lane. audit handoff:fn_to_hp

nodes.title: Where does the hot water come from?
nodes.body: A hot-water air handler has a coil of pipes inside, fed by a boiler or a water heater.
choices: Hydro-air source: tank water heater. flag tankless_lead
A tankless water heater or combi boiler
Hydro-air source: tankless or combi. flag tankless_lead

nodes.title: Check the air side
nodes.body: Hot water is reaching the coil, so the problem is likely on the air side: the blower, the filter, or the air path. Look from outside the unit.

step.source: From First Co HBXBX-HW spec sheet (45-second blower-on delay; Freeze Protector), checked 2026-10-11.
steps: With heat calling, wait one minute and listen for the blower.
Feel a vent for warm air.
Look for water or ice around the unit.
step.watch: About a minute after the heat call starts.
step.stop: Stop if you see water near wires or ice on the unit.

choices: A short wait, then warm air
Air is weak or barely warm
Ice or dripping at the unit, and it's in a cold space

nodes.title: When was the furnace installed?
nodes.body: Two-stage and variable furnaces can run differently depending on the thermostat type and its settings.
choices: In the last year, or it's still under the installer's warranty
Longer ago, or my installer said it's OK

results.title: Leave high vents to a pro
results.exp: The furnace pipes are too high to reach safely from the ground.
act: Call a licensed HVAC pro and say snow or ice may be blocking the furnace vent.
Keep CO alarms on, and leave if one sounds.
results.avoid: Don't use a ladder or go on the roof.

results.title: Don't go out in these conditions
results.exp: Ice, dark, or the storm makes this the wrong time to go outside.
act: Call a licensed HVAC pro or your gas utility and say the vent may be blocked.
Keep CO alarms on, and leave if one sounds.
results.avoid: Don't go out on ice or in the storm to clear vents.

results.title: Call the gas company about the meter
results.exp: The gas meter or propane regulator is buried or iced. Ice there can affect gas pressure.
act: Call your gas utility or propane supplier to report it.
You can brush loose snow off gently with a soft broom.
results.avoid: Don't chip, kick, or melt ice on the meter or regulator.

results.title: Ice is inside or frozen to the pipe
results.exp: The snow came off, but ice stays inside or frozen onto a pipe end.
act: Call a licensed HVAC pro and say a furnace vent pipe is iced.
Keep CO alarms on, and leave if one sounds.
results.avoid: Don't chip, melt, or pour water on the pipes.

results.title: Stop using the furnace
results.exp: A vent pipe outside looks cracked, sagging, or pulled apart. Exhaust could get back inside.
act: Set the thermostat to Off.
Call a licensed HVAC pro today.
Keep CO alarms on, and leave if one sounds.
results.avoid: Don't push pipes back together or tape them.

results.title: Vents clear · heat is back
results.exp: Snow at the pipes was the likely cause. The furnace started again on its own.
act: Check both pipes after every storm and drift.
If it stops again with clear pipes, start a new check.
results.avoid: Don't pile shoveled snow near the pipes.

results.title: The drain line is freezing
results.exp: Ice in the drain tube can back water up and shut a high-efficiency furnace off. It needs freeze protection.
act: Call a licensed HVAC pro and say the condensate drain is frozen.
Ask whether the trap and line need heat tape or a new route.
results.avoid: Don't use a torch, heat gun, or boiling water on it.

results.title: The condensate pump may be full
results.exp: A full or beeping pump can shut the furnace off to stop a leak.
act: Call a licensed HVAC pro or plumber about the condensate pump.
Wipe up water on the floor and keep it away from outlets.
results.avoid: Don't open the pump or furnace to drain it.

results.title: Drain tube straightened · retest
results.exp: A kinked or sagging drain tube can block water and shut the furnace off.
act: Give it up to an hour to try again on its own.
If it stays off or water appears, start a new check.
results.avoid: Don't pull tubes off the furnace or cut them.

results.title: Stop · the code means a flame-safety trip
results.exp: Your code means a safety switch saw heat where flames shouldn't be.
act: Set the thermostat to Off.
Call a licensed HVAC pro today and give them the code.
Keep CO alarms on, and leave if one sounds.
results.avoid: Don't reset anything or open the furnace.
results.src: CAR, ICP, JCI, RH-R95T, TR-S9V2, ALD

results.title: Stop · flame when there shouldn't be
results.exp: Your code means the furnace sensed flame or gas when it wasn't calling for heat.
act: Set the thermostat to Off and call a licensed HVAC pro now.
Smell gas? Leave and call from outside.
results.avoid: Don't open the furnace or touch the gas line.
results.src: CAR, GDM, LNX, JCI, NAP, ICP

results.title: Call a pro and give them the code
results.exp: Your furnace showed code {code}: {code_meaning}.
act: Tell the tech: {code_tell}
Keep the power on so the code stays stored.
results.avoid: Don't reset the furnace or open its doors.

results.title: Match the code to your door label
results.exp: We don't list that code for your brand. Codes change by model and board.
act: Read the code chart on the furnace, or take a photo through the window.
Give the code and model number to a licensed HVAC pro.
results.avoid: Don't remove the door to find the chart.

results.title: A tripped furnace breaker needs a pro
results.exp: A furnace breaker usually trips because of a problem in the furnace.
act: Leave the breaker as it is.
Call a licensed HVAC pro and say the furnace breaker tripped.
results.avoid: Don't reset the breaker or open the furnace.

results.title: Leave the switch the way it is
results.exp: Someone may have turned the furnace switch off on purpose, or you're not sure.
act: Ask who turned it off, and why.
Call a licensed HVAC pro if it was off for a repair, leak, or smell.
results.avoid: Don't turn it back on until you know why it's off.

results.title: Switch back on · heat is back
results.exp: The furnace switch was off by accident. With it on, the furnace started.
act: Mark or cover the switch so nobody flips it by mistake.
If it shuts off again, start a new check.
results.avoid: Don't switch it off and on again to test.

results.title: Out of propane: the supplier checks first
results.exp: Running out can let air into the gas lines. Code requires a leak check before the gas goes back on.
act: Call your propane supplier and say you ran out.
Let them check for leaks and restart your appliances.
results.avoid: Don't open the tank valve or relight anything.

results.title: Order propane now
results.exp: The gauge reads low. Running out stops the furnace and means a leak check before the gas goes back on.
act: Call your propane supplier for a delivery today.
If the furnace still won't heat, start a new check.
results.avoid: Don't touch the tank valves or regulator.

results.title: Out of oil: call for delivery and service
results.exp: An empty tank can draw air or sludge into the burner. It may need a tech after delivery.
act: Call your oil supplier for a delivery and ask about a service visit.
Keep the thermostat on Off until then.
results.avoid: Don't press the red reset button on the burner.

results.title: Oil burner locked out: call a pro
results.exp: The burner control's light says it locked itself out.
act: Call your oil service company and tell them the light color and pattern.
Keep the thermostat on Off until they come.
results.avoid: Don't press the red reset button, even once.

results.title: Filter fixed · retest
results.exp: A wrong-size, doubled-up, or backward filter can choke airflow and shut the furnace off.
act: Use one filter of the size printed on the old one, arrow toward the furnace.
If it still shuts off, start a new check.
results.avoid: Don't stack filters or run without one.

results.title: Air path cleared · retest
results.exp: A mobile-home furnace pulls air through its door louvers. Blocking them starves it.
act: Keep the louvers, grilles, and gaps under doors clear.
Don't store anything in the furnace closet.
If it still shuts off, start a new check.
results.avoid: Don't tape over or cover the louvered door.

results.title: The crossover duct needs a look
results.exp: If the duct between the halves is down, crushed, or loose, heat escapes under the home.
act: Call a manufactured-home installer or HVAC pro about the crossover duct.
Ask them to seal it and strap it off the ground.
results.avoid: Don't crawl under the home to fix it yourself.

results.title: Keep away from animals under the home
results.exp: Animals under the home can damage ducts and wiring.
act: Stay out from under the home.
Call pest control, then an HVAC pro for the ducts.
results.avoid: Don't reach in or crawl under to look.

results.title: Questions for a mobile-home furnace job
results.exp: Furnaces in manufactured homes must be listed for manufactured homes.
act: Ask your installer: is this furnace listed for manufactured homes?
Ask whether the AC or heat pump is certified to pair with it.
results.avoid: Don't buy a standard house furnace for a manufactured home.

results.title: Cool, then warm, can be normal
results.exp: Many electric furnaces turn their heaters on in steps after the fan starts, so air warms over a few minutes.
act: If air gets warm and rooms keep up, no action is needed.
If it never gets warm, start a new check.
results.avoid: Don't open the furnace panel or touch the breaker.

results.title: A short fan delay can be normal
results.exp: Some hot-water air handlers warm the coil before the fan starts, so a short wait is normal.
act: If warm air follows the wait, no action is needed.
If air stays cool, start a new check.
results.avoid: Don't open the air handler.

results.title: The water coil may be freezing
results.exp: Ice or dripping at an air handler in a cold space can mean the coil is freezing.
act: Call a licensed heating pro today and say the hot-water coil may freeze.
Keep the thermostat calling for heat.
results.avoid: Don't press any reset or open the unit.

results.title: Check the thermostat next
results.exp: A new furnace may need thermostat settings changed to match it.
act: Continue to the thermostat check.
Have the furnace model number ready.
results.avoid: Don't change thermostat wiring.

results.title: Ask your installer first
results.exp: A recent install is the installer's to check, and warranties may depend on it.
act: Call your installer and ask the questions on this card.
Give them any code you saw.
results.avoid: Don't change wiring or furnace settings yourself.

reasons: vent_not_pvc
Your furnace vents through a metal pipe, so there are no outdoor plastic pipes to clear.
vent_check_inaccessible
The outdoor vent pipes couldn't be checked safely.
vent_cleared_still_no_heat
The vent pipes are clear, but the heat didn't come back after the wait.
vent_cleared_code_repeats
The furnace stopped again with the same code after the pipes were cleared.
condensate_check_inaccessible
The drain tube couldn't be seen without opening the furnace.
code_limit_after_basics
The code points to overheating, and the filter and vents looked fine.
code_pressure_after_basics
